instance: Source tests passed and a security fix landed in Rust source, but a committed release binary under bin/ was not rebuilt, so the shipped executable still permitted a blocked destructive-command operation for nine days after the source fix; this escaped twice on 2026-07-15.
check: Byte-compare all committed bin/ executables against a fresh canonical rebuild (remapping checkout/target/Cargo-home/sysroot prefixes) and require exact set equality between Cargo targets and committed ELF files.

instance: The codex-github wrapper called gh with --json for subcommands that do not support it (gh pr create, gh pr checks, gh pr merge) or with an unsupported --repo global flag (gh repo view), causing gh_failed errors even though the equivalent raw gh command in text mode succeeds.
check: Add a mock test that rejects unsupported --json/--repo flag usage before changing code; verify raw-CLI parity for each gh subcommand wrapped.

instance: codex-github pr-checks treated a nonzero gh pr checks exit code as a hard failure (gh_failed) even when stdout still contained parseable check-status rows for checks that were merely pending or failing.
check: Parse valid check rows even from nonzero gh pr checks output, preserving hard failure only when no parseable rows are present; test both successful and pending check output.

source_anchor: REST Issue Listing Includes Pull Requests
instance: codex-github list-issues --limit N returned fewer than N issues via REST fallback because GitHub's /issues endpoint mixes issues and pull requests, and per_page was set equal to limit before filtering out pull_request rows, so a page could be exhausted by PR rows and under-return real issues.
check: Fetch enough mixed rows before filtering, then apply --limit after filtering real issues; test mixed payloads where PR rows appear before issue rows.

source_anchor: Remote Shim Readiness Requires Its Own Auth
instance: A launcher's readiness probe against a shim running in token-protected non-loopback mode did not send the required Authorization: Bearer token, so /api/tags returned 401 and the launcher reported startup failure and killed an otherwise-healthy shim.
check: Centralize readiness probes in one helper that adds Authorization when CODEX_OLLA_REMOTE_TOKEN is set; test remote-token and loopback/no-token readiness paths with mocked curl.

source_anchor: Install Surface Drift From Tracked Binaries
instance: make install exposed a stale command with no remaining Cargo source, and a Cargo-declared command was missing from installation, because release/install targets were derived from existing tracked bin/codex-* artifacts rather than from Cargo metadata; bootstrap allowlists, doctor checks, README instructions, and Makefile install targets ended up describing different tool sets.
check: Test Makefile, Cargo [[bin]] targets, bootstrap allowlist, doctor tool checks, and tracked bin/codex-* files for consistency in both directions, including that every declared bin/<name> entry exists and is readable.

source_anchor: Partner QA Is Part Of The Contract
instance: Local tests passed, but partner review (Grok, Hermes, Claude) found an untested edge case that wrapper-first validation exposed and that raw CLI commands had hidden.
check: Treat partner review as required QA before merge; track partner-discovered bugs as issues even when fixed in the same PR; re-run focused partner review after addressing requested changes.

instance: A repository hygiene test failed on generated, editor, or other ignored files because recursive filesystem traversal treated untracked/ignored files as repository source; the same checkout passed after deleting local artifacts despite no tracked change.
check: Enumerate the intended tracked surface with git ls-files -- <pathspecs> instead of walking the filesystem, and fail loudly if Git cannot enumerate the files; test both an ignored artifact and a tracked source file containing the prohibited value.

instance: codex-guard ssh host 'echo <payload> | base64 -d | bash' reported allowed even though the decoded payload contained a command that would be blocked directly (e.g. git push --force), because guard logic checked shell segments split on pipes without seeing the producer, decoder, and shell executor together; lowercasing wrapper tokens before SSH recursion also corrupted case-sensitive encoded payloads.
check: Preserve raw tokens when extracting shell/SSH inner commands; decode only executable base64 pipelines, then recursively inspect the decoded command; keep ordinary non-executed base64 decoding allowed.

source_anchor: Encoded Shell Pipeline Bypasses — Follow-Up Hardening (Issue #110)
instance: Follow-up hardening found: (1) a command chaining two producer|base64 -d|shell pipelines only had its first pipeline decoded, leaving a malicious second pipeline invisible; (2) env bash and /usr/bin/env bash sinks were not recognized as shell interpreters, so producer|base64 -d|env bash bypassed detection; (3) when a producer's output could not be statically decoded (e.g. a python3 -c '...' producer), the guard used ? to bail with None, which the caller treated as 'no pipeline present' and silently allowed the command (fail-open).
check: Scan the entire command for every executable base64 pipeline independently; normalize sink tokens by stripping a leading env wrapper and basenaming path-qualified commands; when the pipeline shape matches but the producer output can't be statically determined, fail CLOSED with a distinct unverifiable_base64_pipeline finding rather than allowing the command.
